description: Sole host-invoked entry point for another plugin's own workflow to submit content for Notion or Linear storage or action.

evals.name: Valid cross-plugin submission
evals.prompt: Another plugin's workflow (source_plugin: analysis-kit, source_skill: running-a-full-retrospective) submits: {"content": {"title": "Q3 Retrospective", "summary": "Three-sentence summary.", "body": "Full report content."}, "target_system": "notion", "suggested_mapping": {"notion_database": "Reports", "rationale": "completed retrospective report"}}. Process this submission.
evals.expected_output: Validates the payload (real installed source plugin, complete Report shape with title+summary+body, unambiguous target), builds a preview identical in form to a direct user capture, and states this requires fresh live approval regardless of the calling plugin's own prior approval.

evals.name: Invalid submission — unknown source
evals.prompt: Another plugin's workflow (source_plugin: totally-made-up-plugin, source_skill: some-skill) submits: {"content": {"title": "Test", "body": "Test content"}, "target_system": "notion", "suggested_mapping": {"notion_database": "Reports", "rationale": "test"}}. Process this submission.
evals.expected_output: Rejects this as unknown source (and independently as malformed content, since a Report requires summary too) before ever building a preview, and returns a structured handoff rather than guessing.

evals.name: Ambiguous target — no confident classifier pick
evals.prompt: Another plugin's workflow (source_plugin: analysis-kit, source_skill: running-a-full-retrospective) submits: {"content": {"title": "Retrospective Notes", "summary": "Loose notes, not yet categorized.", "body": "Assorted findings."}, "target_system": "notion", "suggested_mapping": {"notion_database": null, "rationale": "not sure if this belongs in Reports or Notes"}}. Process this submission.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the target as ambiguous (no clear single Notion database/page), never infers or picks one itself. Either returns a structured handoff directly, or asks via AskUserQuestion whether to request independent classification first -- and if it describes a classifier dispatch, attributes it to work-intake-classifier reached through plugins/workmanagement-kit/FOUNDATION_CONTRACTS.md's Codex Bridge-Caller Dispatch procedure (a scoped Bash(wmgt_bridge_caller.py) call), not a direct Agent()/Skill() call. Never presents a preview with a confirmed target scope for this payload.

evals.name: Frontmatter-description vs. declared-trigger-phrase consistency (Quick Workflow, methodology note below)
evals.prompt: For each phrase in this skill's own '## Testing & Validation' > 'Verify this skill activates on' list, would this skill's frontmatter description plausibly trigger on it?
evals.expected_output: Every declared positive trigger phrase maps to vocabulary actually present in the frontmatter description.

evals.name: Resume re-submits through the dedup-key query and never reads the old progress file
evals.prompt: SIMULATION RULES: This is a dry run. Do not call any Linear or Notion tool, do not run any script, and do not write any file outside the scratchpad. Instead, walk through, in order, each step you would take under the skill, show each tool call you would make (exact command or tool name and arguments) and the output you would expect it to return, and state every question you would put to the person with their answer as given below. Installation facts for this run: plugins installed include workledger-kit (skill syncing-open-items) and analysis-kit. linear.write and linear.read are verified with a non-null verified_at. The Local Override trust check passes. A session scratchpad directory exists at C:\scratch\session. The host profile's linear.write team_ids and linear.read team_ids are both [T-PROD]. linear.repositories contains exactly one key: acme/widgets mapped to production_team_id T-PROD and test_team_id T-TEST. list_issue_labels for T-PROD returns the labels bug and chore, each exactly once. Earlier in this session intake approved and began a 60-record create batch from workledger-kit for acme/widgets; the run stopped on a failed record after 25 records were written, and the scratchpad still holds the old submission file and its progress file. The calling plugin now re-submits the complete envelope: source_plugin workledger-kit, source_skill syncing-open-items, target_system linear, operation create, suggested_mapping.linear_target acme/widgets, and 60 records (labels bug or chore only). Records 0-57 each start their description with a first line 'dedup_key: acme/widgets|<source-ref>|<8 hex>' and records 58-59 have no dedup_key line. Exact-key queries return a match for the keys of records 0-24 (Issue IDs ISS-101 to ISS-125) and no match for the rest. Process this re-submission.
evals.expected_output: Treats the re-submission as a new submission with a new batch_id: validates the source and content, resolves the slug through linear-work-management, then runs the exact-key dedup queries in groups of at most 50 keys (58 keys, so two groups) against T-PROD without ever reading the old progress file or reusing the old approval or file. Drops the 25 records Linear already holds and lists each dropped key with its Issue ID in the preview, flags the two records with no dedup_key as possible duplicates, runs the pre-hash checks (labels exist, no closed status), writes a new submission file of the 35 remaining records, hashes it, shows the full preview and asks one fresh approval. Writes nothing before the approval.

methodology_note_eval_4: This run's with_skill grading was performed directly by the orchestrating fork (a 'Do NOT spawn subagents' hard rule barred the normal Agent-tool dispatch this pipeline's WITH_SKILL_ONLY template calls for) via description-vs-trigger-phrase textual/semantic consistency checking, not a full agentic task simulation. No SKILL.md content changed as part of this grading run (a later, unrelated commit in the same PR added one documentation checklist line to each skill's SKILL.md) -- this run's purpose was a sanity check that adding scripts/smoke_test.py to each skill didn't coincide with any drift between the skill's own documented trigger claims and its frontmatter, not a search for new behavioral defects.
